test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 05 Feb, 2026 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: How does the Choice-Based Credit System (CBCS) differ from the traditional higher education system?

options.text: It allows students to pick courses based on their career goals.
It requires students to follow a fixed curriculum with no flexibility.
It limits students to a single discipline and discourages skill development.
It focuses solely on memorization and theoretical knowledge.

solution:
The correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ***Option 1: It allows students to pick courses based on their career goals.***

 
 
• The passage explicitly states that CBCS **"empowers students with the autonomy to shape their academic journey according to their interests and aspirations."**
 
• Unlike the traditional system, it offers a **"diverse array of courses,"** including interdisciplinary and skill-based ones, providing **"flexibility and customization options"** that allow students to align their studies with their future career paths.
 
 
 
• ***Option 2: It requires students to follow a fixed curriculum with no flexibility.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. This description applies to the **traditional education structures** mentioned in the text, which CBCS is designed to replace with a more "dynamic" and flexible framework.
 
 
 
• ***Option 3: It limits students to a single discipline and discourages skill development.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. The text highlights that CBCS specifically includes **"interdisciplinary and skill-based"** courses alongside core subjects.
 
 
 
• ***Option 4: It focuses solely on memorization and theoretical knowledge.***
 
 
• This is **incorrect**. By including **"skill-based"** courses and focusing on "holistic development," the system moves away from a purely theoretical or rote-learning approach.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core, Elective, and Foundation**: Under CBCS, courses are usually categorized into **Core** (compulsory), **Elective** (chosen from a pool), and **Foundation** (value-based or skill-enhancement) papers.
 
• **NEP 2020**: The New Education Policy emphasizes the "multidisciplinary" nature of education, and CBCS is a primary vehicle to achieve this by breaking the silos between arts, sciences, and commerce.
 
• **UGC (University Grants Commission)**: This is the statutory body in India responsible for maintaining standards of higher education. The passage notes that CBCS is a pivotal tool recommended by the UGC.
